title: Personal Finance
teaser: Map obligations, preserve flexibility, and compare financial choices on the terms that actually matter.
audience: Adult learners building resilient financial habits

legs.title: See the whole position before choosing

stops.label: Separate flows from the balance sheet

sections.title: Cash flow is a period; net worth is a moment
sections.body: Income and expenses describe movement over a chosen period, and their difference is cash flow. Assets and liabilities describe a position at a point in time, and their difference is net worth. Neither replaces the other: valuable but illiquid assets may coexist with a near-term cash shortfall, while positive monthly cash flow may coexist with large debt. Map timing, ownership, obligations, and uncertainty before treating one headline number as the whole story.

sourceAnchor.heading: 1. Build a Financial Map
sourceAnchor.quote: Net worth is a snapshot, while cash flow is a movie.

activities.prompt: A household owns a valuable property but cannot meet a bill due tomorrow without new debt. Which diagnosis is best?

options.text: It may have positive net worth and still face a near-term liquidity shortfall
Positive net worth automatically makes every current bill affordable
The bill proves that the household received no income this period
The property must be classified as a current expense

explanation.text: Net worth counts value at a moment, but it does not show whether that value is accessible before an obligation falls due. The household can be asset-rich and cash-constrained at the same time.

sourceAnchor.heading: 1. Build a Financial Map
sourceAnchor.quote: A person can own valuable assets yet struggle to pay a near-term bill because those assets cannot quickly be converted into money.

activities.prompt: Match each quantity to the role it plays in a financial map.

pairs.right: Income minus expenses over a period
Assets minus liabilities at a point in time
An amount owed or another financial obligation

explanation.text: Cash flow measures movement, while net worth measures a snapshot assembled from assets and liabilities. Keeping their time frames distinct prevents one measure from hiding a different constraint.

sourceAnchor.heading: 1. Build a Financial Map
sourceAnchor.quote: The difference between total assets and total liabilities at a point in time is **net worth**.

stops.label: Match resources to when they are needed

sections.title: Flexibility has value before growth is counted
sections.body: An emergency reserve is liquid value held for necessary surprises or interrupted income. Its amount depends on the volatility of cash flow, obligations, support, and access—not a universal formula. Less liquid resources may offer growth, but they can be unavailable when the goal arrives. Compounding rewards time only under the scenario's assumed return; it does not guarantee a result, and inflation determines what the future balance can buy.

sourceAnchor.heading: 3. Liquidity, Saving, Inflation, and Compounding
sourceAnchor.quote: An **emergency reserve** is liquid value kept for unplanned, necessary expenses or interruptions in income.

activities.prompt: Which reserve design best serves a household with irregular income and a fixed payment due in two months?

options.text: Keep a goal-matched amount accessible and review it against low-income scenarios
Lock every available unit into the highest projected return regardless of access
Use exactly one month of expenses because the same rule fits every household
Exclude the fixed payment because it has not occurred yet

explanation.text: The reserve's purpose is flexibility under disruption, so access, income variability, and the timing of obligations matter more than a universal target or the largest projected return.

sourceAnchor.heading: 3. Liquidity, Saving, Inflation, and Compounding
sourceAnchor.quote: The appropriate reserve is not a universal number.

activities.prompt: Two statements keep projections within their assumptions. One turns a scenario into a promise. Find the impostor.

statements.text: Inflation can make a larger future balance buy less.
Resource access should be matched to when a goal or obligation arrives.
Given enough time, compounding guarantees the projected return.

explanation.text: Compounding describes what happens under stated rates and timing. Actual returns can vary, so more time does not turn a projection into a guarantee.

sourceAnchor.heading: 3. Liquidity, Saving, Inflation, and Compounding
sourceAnchor.quote: Early contributions have more time to grow, but time does not remove risk or guarantee a return.

sections.title: Names and item counts do not reveal the risk
sections.body: Diversification reduces unnecessary dependence only when holdings respond to different underlying drivers; owning many versions of the same exposure is still concentration. It cannot remove broad loss or guarantee profit. Likewise, a financial product is its rights, obligations, cash flows, risks, and services—not its marketing label. Compare alternatives on a common horizon, including fees, access, currencies, adverse scenarios, and who can change the terms. Liquidity remains part of the comparison because a useful asset at the wrong time may not serve the goal.

sourceAnchor.heading: 6. Investing, Return, and Diversification
sourceAnchor.quote: **Diversification** spreads exposure among assets whose outcomes are not perfectly linked.

activities.prompt: Two products share a label. Which comparison is most decision-relevant?

options.text: Compare full cash flows, access, risks, currencies, change rights, and adverse cases on one horizon
Choose the larger headline rate without checking its period or fees
Assume products in the same marketing category have equivalent obligations
Treat the strongest recent return as a guarantee of the next period

explanation.text: A product comparison must expose the actual rights, cash flows, access conditions, and risks on the same basis. A shared name or one advertised number cannot establish equivalence.

sourceAnchor.heading: 7. Comparing Products, Contracts, and Claims
sourceAnchor.quote: A financial product is a bundle of rights, obligations, cash flows, risks, and services.
